title: Cross-platform QA: token alignment, table overflow and scroll-performance regressions on mobile Safari & Firefox
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We observed multiple UI regressions on mobile Safari and Firefox related to design tokens and table components. Issues surfaced during the responsive QA sweep of the redesigned tokens and the recent table refactor (sticky header + virtualized rows). This ticket captures triage notes, repro steps, a proposed mitigation plan, and follow-ups for engineering and design.
acceptance_criteria:
- All listed issues are either fixed or documented with engineering workitems and tests.
- Visual token mismatches (spacing, color, elevation) are reconciled or have design-approved exceptions.
- Table overflow and horizontal scroll behavior is consistent across iOS Safari and Firefox for Android in our supported viewports.
- Scroll/perf regression mitigations reduce jank to parity with baseline (measured with Lighthouse/DevTools CPU trace on representative devices).
- PRs include regression screenshots and UX signoff from Design.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open the UI Kit playground (link in attachments) on iOS Safari (iPhone 12/13) and Android Firefox (Pixel 5) in mobile viewport.
2) Navigate to Components > Tables and enable 'Virtualized rows' + 'Sticky header' toggles.
3) Add ~200 rows via the debug dataset in the playground.
4) Observe horizontal overflow when column resize token is applied at small breakpoints; attempt to scroll horizontally.
5) Switch to Buttons > Primary with focus styles; tab focus ring appears offset in Firefox mobile.
6) Visit Tokens > Spacing and compare the 'compact' token rendering to baseline: vertical alignment shifts in Safari (text baseline vs. token padding).
7) Record CPU trace while scrolling the virtualized table on iOS Safari to reproduce jank.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Initial exploratory pass. Found 3 distinct issues: (A) token-derived padding mismatch in Safari due to subpixel rounding; (B) table overflow at <= 360px when CSS min-width is enforced on column children; (C) focus ring offset in Firefox mobile caused by transform stacking context on an ancestor.

2026-03-04 - Riley Chen: Reproduced A and B in BrowserStack on iPhone 12 / Firefox for Android. Logged engine issue ENG-2041 for potential runtime fix around virtualization container sizing. Created quick CSS workaround for B (flex-basis clamp) to test UX impact.

2026-03-07 - Eng (Samir Patel): ENG-2041 scoped. Kernel: virtualization sets a hard width for offscreen items which doesn't match min-content in some engines. Proposed approach: compute column intrinsic widths in JS and apply as --riw tokens. Will prototype in a branch.

2026-03-09 - Design review (Ava): Prototype of workaround for B looks acceptable but needs automated visual tests. For A, recommended we adjust the token mapping for 'compact-vertical' to use multiples of 2px at small breakpoints to avoid 0.5px rendering. Filed DES-31267 to finalize token values.

2026-03-12 - QA (Maya Kapoor): Performance traces attached show main-thread spikes correlated with layout thrashing on Safari when sticky header toggles are present. Suggested deferring heavy DOM updates and using will-change transform only on the header (avoid transforms on ancestor containers). Added ENG follow-up ENG-2054.
2026-03-14 - Riley Chen: Updated ticket with proposed acceptance criteria and linked PR draft (attachments). Marking as In Progress while engineering prototypes and design reviews occur.
